effectIntent: A fantasy knight deploys a massive holy aegis that reads instantly as a physical protective shield from a strict top-down action-RPG camera while retaining contemporary layered material depth.

silhouette.primaryMass: forward-weighted faceted round shield plate with a broad upper crown and compressed lower point
silhouette.asymmetry: slight forward bias and one broken outer arc prevent a static UI-medallion read
connections: four large directional braces emerge from and overlap the structural rim
the central crest is embedded into the plate and never floats above it
all energy gaps terminate inside the metal frame
motifs: four broad crown-like braces with unequal front and rear weight

depthLayers.role: thin contact shadow and energy seating cue
recessed translucent protective plane with faceted depth
raised gold frame and four connected braces
single restrained focal crest and directional leading highlight

materialZones.finish: deep translucent emerald with slow internal refraction-like flow and nonuniform opacity
warm metal body with narrow moving specular accents and restrained emissive seams
soft dark-green occlusion plus a narrow contact glow, never a full magic circle

forbiddenTraits: particles used to hide weak geometry
literal copying of any reference motif
acceptanceQuestions: At gameplay scale, does the primary shield plate read before the crest and braces?
From strict top view, do overlap, value, and negative space create physical depth rather than a flat icon?
Are all four braces visibly load-bearing parts of the rim rather than detached glyphs?
Does the silhouette remain authored and attractive with all Shader color removed?
Does the color concept feel current for a modern indie action RPG rather than an older handheld title?
Can the caster and target remain readable through the shield plane?
